_comment: Everything that makes the data a function of calendar time rather than a stationary process. Without this file the generator draws visit dates uniformly over the observation window, which produces flat monthly counts, a constant telehealth share and codes that appear before they were issued. Real longitudinal data has none of those properties, and the absence of them is what makes a synthetic extract unusable for testing time-series or seasonality logic.

seasonality_profiles._comment: Monthly multipliers on event intensity, January first. Each profile is normalised to mean 1.0 by the loader, so a profile only changes *when* events happen, never how many.

visit_seasonality._comment: Applied to routine/surveillance visits that are not driven by a specific condition. The December bump is deductible exhaustion: US patients who have met their out-of-pocket maximum schedule elective care before the plan year resets. The January trough is the mirror image.

volume._comment: Multiplier on overall encounter intensity by calendar year, interpolated linearly between anchor points. Captures three real forces: (a) a health system's EHR coverage grows as sites are onboarded, so early years are thinner; (b) COVID suppressed non-urgent care in 2020 then rebounded through deferred-care catch-up in 2021-22; (c) the final months of any extract are right-censored because claims and results have not finished settling. The trailing shelf is applied separately.

censoring._comment: Records in the last N days before the extract date are progressively less likely to have landed: labs resulted late, claims still adjudicating, discharge summaries unsigned. A flat cliff at the end of an extract is one of the clearest tells that data is synthetic.

visit_mix._comment: Share of encounters by visit type at each anchor date, interpolated linearly. Shares are renormalised after interpolation, so they need not sum to exactly 1. Telehealth is the important one: essentially nonexistent before March 2020, a near-vertical spike when CMS relaxed originating-site rules, then a partial retreat to a new plateau far above baseline. Any tool tested on data with a constant telehealth share will silently fail on real post-2020 data.

vocabulary_windows._comment: When each fictitious code family was issued and retired. A code emitted outside its window is an anachronism, and anachronisms are the single easiest way for a reviewer to prove a dataset is fabricated. DXCODE9 is the legacy classification retired at the 2015-10-01 cutover; DXCODE replaces it. Note the retirement is not a hard stop - see cutover_tail.

cutover._comment: The DXCODE9 -> DXCODE transition. Real transitions are not instantaneous: a minority of sites keep submitting legacy codes for months afterwards through unconverted interfaces and back-dated encounters. tail_days is how long stragglers persist and tail_rate is the share of diagnoses still coded legacy immediately after cutover, decaying linearly to zero. This is a *deliberate* quirk, documented in KNOWN_QUIRKS.md.

pandemic._comment: COVID-19 cannot exist before it existed. The generator hard-clamps every covid19 onset, test, vaccine and related code to this window - the clamp is applied *after* all date perturbation, not before, because an earlier version applied it first and a later 'surface censored onset during follow-up' step then re-drew the date uniformly from the coverage window and put COVID cases back into 2010.

error_budget._comment: Deliberately injected defects, at rates the consuming tool is expected to survive. Every one of these is counted exactly during generation and written to ground_truth.json under 'injected_errors', which turns them from noise into known-answer tests: a data-quality checker that reports 0.5% out-of-period records is correct, and one that reports 0% has a bug. Set every rate to 0 with --messiness clean.
